The application boundary enforces a dual-layered structure: personal learning (L) and public-facing application (A), constrained by owner approval (O). This creates a conditional probability space where artifacts are only released when O=1. The repo-safe summary (S) acts as a kernel function that abstracts sensitive data into a form suitable for public consumption. Public narrative discipline (N) emerges as a consequence of this abstraction, strengthening the coherence of operational storytelling. Failure occurs when L>A without proper boundary enforcement, leading to unauthorized disclosure. The system exhibits a duality between internal knowledge and external presentation, governed by a binary approval mechanism. In GSE context, this translates to a state transition model where pre-approval states yield to validated artifact states through boundary checks.
